claims.text: A hydride-precursor route can be used to produce an Nb-Mo-Ta-W-V-Ti refractory high-entropy alloy.
Ball-milled NbMoTaWVTi powder can contain approximately 0.86 wt% oxygen.
The initial mixture of hydride precursors and refractory metal powders has a BCC solid-solution structure.
Heating at 600–800 °C is sufficient to decompose the hydride precursors and release hydrogen without leaving problematic residual hydrogen.
Maintaining a pressure below 10^-6 Pa during hydride decomposition prevents oxygen uptake and re-oxidation.
SPS at 1400 °C can consolidate NbMoTaWVTi powder to approximately 96.75% relative density.
Oxygen introduced during processing of NbMoTaWVTi can produce an FCC TiO precipitated phase during SPS.
Oxygen uptake in Nb-Mo-Ta-W-V-Ti leads to precipitation of brittle alpha-HCP phases.
Relatively high oxygen content can promote brittleness and cracking during deformation of Group-IV-containing refractory high-entropy alloys.
Vacuum hydride decomposition will maintain a single-phase or coherent BCC matrix in Nb-Mo-Ta-W-V-Ti after SPS.
The proposed route will produce a BCC matrix with grain size below 1.35 μm.
TiO precipitates act as brittle crack-initiation sites in NbMoTaWVTi.
The proposed hydride route will yield greater than 96% relative density.
The proposed route will produce bulk material without catastrophic cracking.
Vacuum hydride decomposition followed by SPS will eliminate FCC TiO precipitates.
The resulting alloy will have compressive yield strength exceeding 2700 MPa.
A yield strength above 2700 MPa can be achieved through solid-solution and grain-boundary strengthening without TiO precipitation strengthening.
Conventional mechanical alloying followed by SPS can cause oxygen uptake and FCC TiO formation in NbMoTaWVTi.
Conventional powder processing of NbMoTaWVTi causes cracking during consolidation or subsequent deformation because of oxygen-induced embrittlement.
Suppressing metastable oxide or HCP phases will enhance high-temperature yield strength relative to direct powder mixing.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described simultaneously as a physical mixture of undecomposed hydrides and elemental metal powders and as a BCC solid solution. The cited work only obtains BCC solid solutions after extended mechanical alloying, not in the initial precursor blend.

The hypothesis predicts enhanced strength after eliminating TiO, but the cited conventional-route alloy already has a 2709 MPa yield strength and explicitly attributes part of that strength to TiO precipitation. Merely predicting greater than 2700 MPa does not establish improvement over that baseline.
